---
title: "Player bio construction"
format: html
execute:
  echo: true
---

This reproducible report creates only the player-level `data/player_bio.csv`
from the approved player sources and the father-son family list. It deliberately
does not read salary values into the output, and does not use height/weight or
the prior merging script.

```{r}
inputs <- c("data/all_seasons.csv",
  "data/archive_wyatt/csv/common_player_info.csv",
  "data/NBA Player Salaries_2000-2025.csv",
  "data/father_son_list.csv",
  "data/nba_siblings_list.csv")
stopifnot(all(file.exists(inputs)))
file.info(inputs)[, c("size", "mtime")]
input_counts <- data.frame(source = basename(inputs),
  rows = vapply(inputs, function(path) nrow(read.csv(path)), integer(1)))
input_counts
```

```{r}
system2("Rscript", "scripts/create_player_bio.R")
bio <- read.csv("data/player_bio.csv", check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
review <- read.csv("results/player_bio_review.csv", check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
family_verification <- read.csv("results/father_son_verification.csv",
  check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
family_relations <- read.csv("data/family_relations.csv",
  check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
```

The script uses `common_player_info` as the authoritative register when a
name matches. A unique valid normalized name found only in `all_seasons.csv`
is included with a deterministic fallback ID and `other_flag = 1`; its
identity fields come only from the deduplicated season rows. Salary-only names
are not added to the bio table and remain review findings. Names in
`father_son_list.csv` absent from all player sources are added as blank bio rows
with deterministic IDs, so every listed relationship can be represented.
Father/son flags and connected `familyID` values are assigned from the family
list. Suffixes are
preserved in output names; only an internal normalized key removes them.
School selection is the first deterministic non-missing `all_seasons$college`
value, then `common_player_info$school`. Missing birthdates are reported but
are not treated as identity conflicts.

```{r}
expected <- c("playerID","first_name","last_name","full_name","school","country",
  "draft_year","draft_round","draft_number","familyID","father_dummy","son_dummy",
  "brother_dummy","twin_dummy","birthdate","greatest_75_flag","same_name_flag","other_flag")
stopifnot(identical(names(bio), expected),
          !anyDuplicated(bio$playerID),
          all(nzchar(bio$playerID)), all(nzchar(bio$full_name)),
          all(nzchar(bio$first_name)), all(nzchar(bio$last_name)),
          all(bio$brother_dummy %in% 0:1, bio$twin_dummy %in% 0:1),
          all(bio$same_name_flag %in% 0:1), all(bio$other_flag %in% 0:1))
stopifnot(nrow(family_verification) == nrow(read.csv("data/father_son_list.csv")),
          all(family_verification$status %in% c("linked", "linked_ambiguous_name")),
          all(family_verification$father_exists),
          all(family_verification$son_exists),
          all(family_verification$father_dummy_ok),
          all(family_verification$son_dummy_ok),
          all(family_verification$shared_familyID))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(family_relations$relation_ID),
          all(family_relations$status %in% c("linked", "linked_ambiguous_name")),
          all(family_relations$familyID > 0),
          !anyDuplicated(family_relations[family_relations$relation_type == "sibling",
                                          c("familyID", "person1_playerID", "person2_playerID")]),
          all(family_relations$person1_match_count > 0),
          all(family_relations$person2_match_count > 0))
stopifnot(any(grepl("Jr\\.?|Sr\\.?|\\b(II|III|IV|V)\\b", bio$full_name)))
fallback <- grepl("^fallback_", bio$playerID)
stopifnot(all(bio$other_flag[fallback] == 1),
          all(is.na(bio$birthdate[fallback]) | !nzchar(bio$birthdate[fallback])),
          all(bio$familyID[fallback] == 0))
summary(data.frame(players = nrow(bio),
  fallback_players = sum(fallback),
  same_name_players = sum(bio$same_name_flag == 1),
  other_flag_players = sum(bio$other_flag == 1),
  missing_birthdate = sum(is.na(bio$birthdate) | !nzchar(bio$birthdate)),
  review_rows = nrow(review)))
table(review$issue_type)
```

All findings (duplicate names, unmatched/ambiguous names, school conflicts,
and invalid or missing dates) are consolidated in
`results/player_bio_review.csv`. The per-relation verification is saved in
`results/father_son_verification.csv`; the script stops if any listed father
or son is missing, incorrectly flagged, or lacks a shared non-zero `familyID`.
Rows with duplicate matching names receive status `linked_ambiguous_name` and
remain flagged for manual review rather than being silently treated as unique.
The relation table `data/family_relations.csv` contains one row per
father--son or sibling pair. `relation_ID` identifies the individual relation,
while `familyID` identifies the complete family. Father--son rows preserve
direction; sibling pairs are stored only once.
Sibling pairs are taken both from the explicit sibling source and, when two
sons share a father in `father_son_list.csv`, from the derived shared-father
rule. The `source` column distinguishes these cases.
